_doc: Goya · epilogue, Bordeaux (1825–1828): three letters, two to Joaquín María Ferrer in Paris and his last lines to his son Javier. Talks: e1 with Moratín (talk.me), whose public-domain letters about Goya in Bordeaux are quoted in Beruete 1916, pp. 145–151; the Duchess of Alba never speaks. Spanish = modern spelling (accents, b/v, h, x/j, joined words, abbreviations written out; no rewording and no change of word order), each message keeps the text as printed in the public-domain edition in orig.es (shown in the app as an optional ‘original spelling’ line). Editors' interjections are removed; nothing is taken from the 1981/82 or 2003 editions or their notes. verified=false: checked against the archive.org full text, a last check against the page images is still to do. en · ko translated from the Spanish for this app. Replies and talks are written by this app, not by the recipients.

head.es: (Desde Burdeos, a París, 6 de diciembre de 1825)

letters.excerpt: Messages 0–1 are the passage Beruete prints (it begins mid-letter, marked …). His postscript after 'Vivo Rue Croix Blanche núm. 10', 'Y si nos morimos q.e nos entierren', is quoted in the note, not as a message.

messages.es: …Con motivo de ir a París el señor de Baranda, le enviaba a usted un ensayo litográfico que representa una fiesta de novillos, a fin de que la viese usted y el amigo Cardano, y, si la encontraban digna de despacharse algunas, enviaría las que usted quisiere.
messages.en: …As Señor de Baranda was going to Paris, I sent you by him a trial lithograph showing a fight with young bulls, so that you and our friend Cardano could see it, and, if you found it worth selling a few, I would send as many as you wished.
messages.ko: …바란다 씨가 파리에 간다기에, 어린 소 투우 장면을 그린 석판화 시험작을 한 장 보냈어요. 당신과 친구 카르다노가 보고, 몇 장 팔 만하다 싶으면 원하는 만큼 보내 드리려고요.

messages.en: I put this note inside the print, and, having had no news, I beg you again to let me know, because I have made three more of the same size and on the subject of bulls.

note.ko: 1824년 6월, 일흔여덟의 고야는 온천 요양 허가를 받아 스페인을 떠났어요. 보르도에 들른 그를 보고 친구 모라틴은 ‘귀먹고 늙고 굼뜨고 약한데, 프랑스 말은 한마디도 모르면서 세상 구경에 들떠 있다’고 썼어요. 고야는 파리를 다녀온 뒤 보르도에 머물렀고, 1825년 투우를 그린 큰 석판화 네 장을 만들었어요. 받는 사람 페레르는 파리에 사는 스페인 사람으로, 1824년 고야가 파리에서 초상을 그려 준 친구예요. 이 편지 끝에 고야는 주소 ‘크루아 블랑슈 거리 10번지’와 함께 ‘우리가 죽으면 묻어 주겠지’라는 한 줄을 덧붙였어요.
note.en: In June 1824 Goya, aged seventy-eight, left Spain with leave to take the waters. When he stopped in Bordeaux his friend Moratín wrote that he had arrived ‘deaf, old, clumsy and weak, without a word of French … and so happy and so eager to see the world’. After a stay in Paris he settled in Bordeaux, and in 1825 he made four large lithographs of bullfights. Ferrer was a Spaniard living in Paris, a friend whose portrait Goya had painted there in 1824. After his address, ‘Rue Croix Blanche no. 10’, Goya added one line to this letter: ‘And if we die, let them bury us.’
note.source: A. de Beruete y Moret, Goya, grabador (Madrid, 1918), p. 156–157 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/AV194 ; A. de Beruete y Moret, Goya, pintor de retratos (Madrid, 1916), p. 145–147 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/AV192 ; image: see plate.imageSource

letters.excerpt: Messages 0–1 are the passage Beruete prints; the separator '==' between them is left out. 'más ha de 20 años' (archaic for 'hace más de 20 años') stays as written. In the app text S. M. is written out (Su Majestad).

messages.es: Quedo enterado y convencido de lo que usted me dice de las estampas de toros; pero, como yo pensé más en que las viesen los conocedores artísticos que en esa gran corte abundan, y también la gran porción de gente que las habrá visto, sin contar el número de españoles, creí que era fácil, dándolas a un estampero sin decir mi nombre, y a poco precio, podía haberse hecho.
messages.en: I've taken in what you tell me about the bull prints, and I'm convinced; but since I was thinking more of the art connoisseurs, who abound in that great capital, and also of the great many people who will have seen them, not counting the Spaniards, I thought it was easy: by giving them to a print-seller without saying my name, and at a low price, it could have been done.
messages.ko: 투우 판화에 대해 하신 말씀, 잘 알아들었고 수긍해요. 그래도 저는 그 큰 도시에 많은 미술 감식가들, 그리고 그 판화를 봤을 많은 사람들을 생각했어요. 스페인 사람들은 빼고도요. 그래서 제 이름은 밝히지 않고 판화 장수에게 싸게 넘기면 쉽게 될 줄 알았어요.

messages.es: Lo que me dice usted de los Caprichos no puede ser, porque las láminas las cedí al Rey más ha de 20 años, como las demás cosas que he grabado, que están en la Calcografía de Su Majestad.
messages.en: What you tell me about the Caprichos cannot be, because I gave the plates to the King more than twenty years ago, like the other things I have engraved, which are in His Majesty's Calcografía.

note.ko: 페레르의 답장은 남아 있지 않지만, 파리에서 투우 판화를 팔기는 어렵다는 말이었던 것 같아요. 고야가 《카프리초스》 동판을 왕께 바친 것은 1803년, 스물두 해 전이에요(VI장). 1918년 베루에테는 프랑스의 폴 르포르가 보르도의 투우 석판화를 들라크루아의 석판화와 견주었다고 적었어요. 들라크루아는 고야의 판화를 여러 점 가지고 있었어요. 모라틴은 1825년 봄 ‘고야는 이 도시와 들판, 날씨, 먹을거리, 자유와 고요를 좋아한다’고 썼어요.
note.en: Ferrer's reply is lost, but it seems he had said the bull prints would be hard to sell in Paris. Goya had given the Caprichos plates to the King in 1803, twenty-two years before (chapter VI). In 1918 Beruete noted that the Frenchman Paul Lefort had compared the Bordeaux bullfight lithographs with Delacroix's lithographs, and that Delacroix owned several of Goya's prints. In the spring of 1825 Moratín wrote that Goya liked ‘the city, the country, the climate, the food, the independence, the quiet he enjoys’.

letters.dateNote: Undated. Written in bed after the news that Javier was coming to Bordeaux (Beruete 1916, p. 154; Viñaza 1887, p. 69); Goya died in Bordeaux on 16 April 1828 (the records do not agree on whether Javier arrived in time, so the app does not say). Spring 1828; no modern dating checked.
letters.ref: Beruete 1916, p. 154 (also Viñaza 1887, p. 69) · A. de Beruete y Moret, Goya, pintor de retratos (Madrid, 1916), p. 154 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/AV192
letters.excerpt: Messages 0–2 are the whole note. Beruete prints the signature 'Fco.'. The grandson Mariano's line written just before it and his note at the foot are quoted in the note, not as messages.

messages.es: Querido Javier: No te puedo decir más que de tanta alegría me he puesto un poco indispuesto y estoy en la cama.

note.ko: 1826년 고야는 마드리드에 잠시 다녀와 은퇴를 허락받았고, 다시 보르도로 돌아왔어요. 1828년 봄, 아들 하비에르가 보르도에 온다는 소식을 듣고 고야는 너무 기뻐 앓아누웠어요. 손자 마리아노가 먼저 ‘아빠, 할아버지가 몇 자 적으실 거예요’라고 쓰고, 그 아래 고야가 직접 이 몇 줄을 적었어요. 편지 끝에 마리아노는 ‘할아버지가 쓴 마지막 글’이라고 적어 두었어요. 1828년 4월 16일, 고야는 보르도에서 여든둘의 나이로 세상을 떠났어요.
note.en: In 1826 Goya made a short trip to Madrid, was allowed to retire, and returned to Bordeaux. In the spring of 1828, on hearing that his son Javier was coming to Bordeaux, he was so overjoyed that he took to his bed. His grandson Mariano first wrote ‘Dear Papa: Grandfather is going to write you a few lines’, and below it Goya wrote these lines himself. At the foot Mariano noted: ‘The last lines Grandfather wrote.’ On 16 April 1828 Goya died in Bordeaux, aged eighty-two.
note.source: A. de Beruete y Moret, Goya, pintor de retratos (Madrid, 1916), p. 154 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/AV192 ; Conde de la Viñaza, Goya, su tiempo, su vida, sus obras (Madrid, 1887), p. 69–70 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/goyasutiemposuv01vinagoog ; image: see plate.imageSource

why.ko: 고야가 보르도에서 마지막 무렵 그린 그림이에요. 1916년 베루에테는 보르도 시절의 ‘아주 아름다운 인물화’로 이 그림을 꼽았어요.
why.en: A painting from Goya's last years in Bordeaux; in 1916 Beruete singled it out among the figures he painted there as ‘tan preciosa’.
